sentences.text: Taohelong possessed a sacral shield, a carpet of osteoderms covering the hips similar to those found in other ankylosaurians.
The neural channel of its tail vertebra has a cross-section shaped like an inverted trapezium.
The outer rim of the ilium has a profile resembling a mirrored 'S' when viewed from the top.
The osteoderms making up the sacral shield are irregular in both their shape and size.
Taohelong was named and described in 2013 by Yang Jing-Tao, You Hai-Lu, Li Da-Qing, and Kong De-Lai.
The only known fossil was discovered in the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin near the border of Yongjing and Lintao counties by the Gansu Zhendan Dinosaur Culture Communication Company.
The genus name refers to the Tao River, while the species name jinchengensis references the ancient name of Lanzhou, Jincheng, meaning 'solid' to describe the animal's armor.
Taohelong is classified within the family Nodosauridae, specifically in the subfamily Polacanthinae.
Phylogenetic analysis identifies Taohelong as the sister taxon to Polacanthus foxii, making it the first described polacanthine from Asia.

While one estimate suggests Taohelon lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, spanning from 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago, other analyses place it more narrowly in the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 110 million years ago in the Aptian stage.
A sauropod distinct from Huanghetitan and Daxiatitan was found 200 meters away from the fossil site within the Hekou Group.
